_comment: Capability matrix for media, server history and server-side tool work (#5227).
One row per provider capability the quote layer can be asked to bound.
Every 'admitted' row names what ENFORCES its maximum and the published source behind it.
Every 'refused' row names the stable refusal reason and the prerequisite that would unblock it.
test_quote_capability_matrix.py asserts the real adapters behave as each row states,
so a row cannot drift from the code. Regenerate rather than hand-edit numbers.

detail: Every money field in the published snapshot and in the curated non-OpenAI table is a
per-1000-token rate. There is no per-call, per-search, per-image, per-minute, per-hour or
per-session fee field anywhere. The source parsers reject non-token pricing tables outright
pricing_policy/aws_sources.py requires a '1K tokens' unit on catalog SKUs), and the snapshot
provenance records the reserved hourly tables as an explicit exclusion.
This absence is the decisive fact for the server_tools rows: with no published rate there is
no arithmetic that yields a ceiling, so those rows are refused rather than estimated.

published_context_ceiling: The bound reserves the model's ENTIRE published context window at the dearest published
input-side rate. This is a provider-enforced maximum, not a prediction: the provider rejects a
request whose assembled input exceeds the model's context window. No deployed endpoint here
publishes a token-counting API, and a client-supplied count is never accepted as evidence.
request_digest: ProviderQuote.request_sha256 is a SHA-256 over the exact bytes forwarded upstream. Content
covered by it cannot change between quoting and submission; binds() refuses the spend if it does.

rows.trusted_count: none pre-flight; the full published context window is reserved instead
rows.rate_source: snapshot.rates + live generation rows, dearest input/cache-write variant
evidence: Media tokens land in the same context window already reserved in full, priced by the same
published per-token rates; the evidence carries no separate per-image or per-page media fee.
Inline bytes are covered by the quote's request digest, so they cannot change after quoting.

payload_requirement: The payload requirement is keyed to the part's declared type: each part must carry its
OWN readable bytes. image_url/file_data are strings and must be an inline 'data:' URI.
input_audio is a nested object {data: '<base64>', format: 'wav'|'mp3'} — the API defines
no 'audio_url' field, and the nested shape has no URL field at all, so base64 there is
structurally inline: in the body and under the request digest.
A media part may carry ONLY the other keys the API defines for it (detail, filename,
prompt_cache_breakpoint); any unrecognised key is refused rather than ignored. This is an
allowlist because the body is forwarded byte-for-byte, so an undocumented *_url/*_id key
would still reach the provider and be dereferenced under the shared principal.

rows.trusted_count: none pre-flight; the full published context ceiling is reserved instead
rows.max_bound_source: model card context_tiers and rate-row max_input_tokens, maximum of both
rows.rate_source: snapshot.rates + live generation rows, dearest input/cache-write variant
evidence: Same reasoning as anthropic_inline_media. A model publishing no context ceiling (the gpt-oss
family) is already refused UNPUBLISHED_CONTEXT_BOUND by the adapter's ceiling lookup, so media
cannot be admitted on a model whose input side has no evidenced maximum.

responses_payload_schemes: any string that is not the full inline form data:<mediatype>;base64,<payload-that-decodes>
a scheme-only match is not enough: data://host/x and data:,https://host/x name somewhere else
input_shapes_refused.refused_on_every_part_not_only_media_par: a reference field (file_id/file_url) is refused on ANY content part, including input_text: the payload rules live in the media branch, but that branch is reached only for a media type, so a text part carrying a reference was previously never inspected while the body is forwarded byte-for-byte
input_shapes_refused.refused_beside_verified_inline_bytes: an unrecognised key on a media part, on an Anthropic media block, or inside an Anthropic source (url, file_id, s3Location, another type's payload field) is refused even when a valid inline payload is present -- verified bytes do not license the rest of the object
input_shapes_refused.inline_payloads_must_decode: a payload documented as base64 must actually decode with validate=True; the base64 alphabet contains + / and =, so a character-class test admits path- and key-shaped references such as file/VICTIM/secret== that name content the gateway does not hold
input_shapes_refused.allowlisted_keys_are_value_checked: format must be wav|mp3, detail must be auto|low|high, filename must be a plain name: an allowlisted key is still caller-controlled and still forwarded byte-for-byte

why_unboundable: NOT for the intuitive reason. Because the bound reserves the whole published context window
and counts nothing, a referenced file's tokens are as enclosed by that reservation as inline
bytes are: on money alone these rows would be admittable. Two other requirements disqualify them.
Authorization: the provider dereferences the name under the gateway's single shared IRSA
principal, so honouring a file_id would let one tenant read content another tenant uploaded --
the same defect that blocks server_retained_history, and a cost ceiling does not fix it.
No fetcher: inspecting what a caller-controlled URL names would mean adding a general URL
fetcher to the quote path, making a pricing component an SSRF surface. #5227 excludes that, so
the reference is refused without being dereferenced.
A mutable reference also cannot be bound by the request digest, so the identity the quote
commits to would not describe what the provider actually reads.
Because the refusal is an authorization control rather than a cost one, it must hold wherever a
reference can appear -- not only where media is priced. Confining the scan to the media branch left
a text-typed part carrying a file_id admitted, which is the same access this row exists to refuse.
rows.prerequisite: per-tenant scoping of provider-stored file ids, or content-addressed references bound into the request digest

why_unboundable: The deployed route does not serve these modalities, so there is no accepted input shape to
price. Refusing by name keeps them from being priced as though they were images.
rows.prerequisite: provider support for the modality on this route, plus a published rate

why_unboundable: The COST side is satisfiable: a provider reassembling stored prior turns does so into the
same context window it enforces, so the unreadable history would sit inside the full-window
reservation, and history mutating after the quote could not break a bound that never depended
on its contents.
The AUTHORIZATION side is not. The issue requires history to be resolved within the same
authorization boundary. Upstream Responses calls are SigV4-signed with the gateway pod's own
IRSA credentials -- one shared principal for every tenant -- and nothing scopes provider-side
stored-response state per tenant: the only body rewrite is a geographic model prefix, tenant
identity reaches AWS at most as a CloudTrail session tag that is explicitly not an
authorization input, and the optional routing override may map two organizations to one
account. Admitting a stored-response reference would let one tenant name an id minted by
another. A correct cost ceiling would not make that access safe.
'background' is refused separately and independently: its final usage arrives after the
response returns, so no trusted in-band usage exists to settle the hold against.
prerequisite: Gateway-side ownership of response ids (persist response_id -> owning tenant at settlement and
reject any previous_response_id not owned by the caller), or provider evidence that response-id
lookup is scoped per principal. Both are outside this issue's scope.
unresolved_external_facts: The provider-side default for the 'store' parameter on this endpoint.
Whether the provider scopes response-id lookup to the calling principal or account.

anthropic_tool_types: any type other than absent or 'custom'

why_unboundable: A provider-run tool bills a per-call fee. No per-call, per-search or per-hour rate exists in
any published source the gateway reads (see pricing_evidence above), so there is no arithmetic
that produces a ceiling for it.
The chargeable work is also not a single unit: the provider may invoke a tool repeatedly within
one request and tool results can drive further model turns, so call count, per-call fees, tool
tokens and recursive work would all need bounding together.
Neither escape hatch is legitimate. A caller-supplied maximum is not provider enforcement -- a
client must never price its own request. A gateway-mediated bounded step loop fixes the step
COUNT but still leaves each step's fee unpriced, so the ceiling would remain unenforceable.
Client-executed tools are unaffected: a 'function'/'custom' declaration is ordinary input
tokens already inside the context bound, and stays admitted.
rows.prerequisite: a published per-call rate for each server-side tool, plus a provider-enforced ceiling on invocations per request

remaining_limitations_for_5175: server_retained_history: refused. Blocked on tenant ownership of provider-side response ids, NOT on cost.
server_side_tools_and_mcp: refused for every provider. Blocked on published per-call rates; no gateway-side workaround exists.
Passing these negative tests is not delivery of the positive capability; both rows stay open on the parent.
